title: fix(gateway): preserve worker inventory after refused database opens
body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/155788

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes worker provisioning becoming stuck with `Worker environment inventory has closed` after an independent database-open attempt is refused.

## User Impact

An admitted inventory stays usable through ordinary open refusals, including transient contention. Explicit closure, terminal failures, and durable quarantine still revoke it. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

A diagnostic open error does not retire the inventory's independent admission. Inventory now follows authoritative lifecycle events. Fresh-open quarantine discovery publishes terminal retirement from the database owner; the obsolete quarantine admission helper is removed. Existing read authority and write-commit checks remain intact.

This extends @meska's contention repair and preserves contributor ancestry and the real interprocess-lock regression. Final scope: eleven files; production net -4 lines, tests net +292 lines. No schema, configuration, or public API changes.

The accompanying fixture corrections are test-only:

- Task-history cleanup drains native state before synchronous registry reset.
- Telegram teardown aborts owned transport before upstream's update-handler join and runtime/database reset.
- Factory-disposal tests join their owned phase promises through the existing test cancellation signal. Three independent one-second phase guards are removed; the overall test deadline and every lifecycle assertion remain.
- The Windows PTY fixture copies Node across volumes instead of requiring a hard link, and one file-level teardown owns all temporary directories.
- Three Gateway completion/setup checks join their existing execution owner before reading the terminal result. The real-handler concurrent-waiter test retains its untracked case and adds explicit agent/chat cases, preserving live wake-up coverage without lifecycle events. The separate in-flight timeout assertion is unchanged.

The workspace-ref test also gains a bounded, failure-only scalar receipt. Its Windows timeout is still unlocalized: this is diagnostic coverage, not a claimed repair. Existing promises, waits, assertions, errors and deadlines remain unchanged; no paths, payloads or environment values are logged.

The branch incorporates frozen main `4d1c5d19ecc893ecef7b52cf7b3be002c794e770`, including canonical [recap publication](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156003), Gateway terminal publication, [Telegram idle-socket](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156466), [Telegram update ownership](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156482), and subagent completion fixture repairs ([#156521](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156521), [#156624](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156624), [#156685](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156685), [owned cleanup](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/1f067fa03de)). It also takes the canonical [Workshop clock repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/764c9331a31b4b87bdc06b95f39c6870c5aca2f3) and [foreground task-publication join](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c947420a323614f7b0d637652d238f2c5db965bd) verbatim. The parent-only fake clock caused a timer overflow and a spurious lease-loss abort. Equivalent earlier fixture work came from [PR #156768](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156768); its author-preserving commits remain in the ancestry, with no duplicate final diff. Original behavioral assertions remain.

## Evidence

- Both database boundaries failed before repair: an ordinary native ownership refusal wrongly closed inventory, while durable quarantine discovery failed to revoke it. The unchanged production repair passed 65 focused inventory, projection, recovery, quarantine, admission and generation tests on its earlier base.
- Earlier hosted proof verified 49 actual case results: [17 inventory](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35839814512/job/107114663435), [9 terminal persistence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35839814512/job/107114662897), [7 abort authorization](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35839814512/job/107114663110), and [16 task history](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35839814512/job/107114663578). These are prior-head supporting evidence.
- Prior matched Linux x64 / Node 24.20.0 proof passed the original Telegram group (211/211 cases) and recap group (180/180 cases). The final branch retains the subsequently landed canonical fixtures.
- The factory-disposal repair passed all 21 cases across its five-case file and two maintenance siblings on Linux x64 / Node 24.20.0 / Vitest 5.0.1; wrapper wall time 57.17 s. All original ownership, ordering and release-failure assertions remain.
- Two-file Windows-fixture formatting and targeted lint passed with zero warnings or errors. Scoped, independent and maintainer reviews found no actionable issues. Linux static checks do not establish Windows runtime success.
- Supporting proof on the identical Workshop fixture passed all 50 cases on Linux x64 / Node 24.20.0 / Vitest 5.0.1, including the original rejection/quarantine case; file wall time 18.02 s, wrapper 19.66 s.
- Supporting proof of the earlier equivalent foreground-publication barrier passed all eight cases on Linux x64 / Node 24.20.0 / Vitest 5.0.1; file wall time 43.33 s, wrapper 45.88 s. Final source takes the independently reviewed upstream terminal-status observer and test-signal join.
- The two Gateway files passed all 104 cases on Linux x64 / Node 24.20.0 / Vitest 5.0.1, including the three original WS cases and all three concurrent-waiter variants; Vitest wall 165.66 s, wrapper 168.06 s. Formatting, targeted lint and scoped review passed.
- Current head `6613855f2cf9885370714328f055b634d8553a94`: [CI attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35928395641/attempts/2) completed successfully (134 successful jobs, 17 skipped). All five Windows lanes, required type/lint jobs and the aggregate gate passed. [ClawSweeper revision 16](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155875#issuecomment-5781282058) reviewed this exact head with no findings, security findings, before-merge items or rank-up moves.
- The single failed Windows packaging job and its dependent aggregate were replayed once without source, assertion or deadline changes. The original TextSnapshot negative case passed in 7.427 s; its tooling group passed 138 cases with 17 skips, and all seven Windows job shards passed. The raw replay checked out synthetic `dd4aaa09eea16b09bfd560c542b73175ff0873f8`, with parents frozen `4d1c5d19ecc893ecef7b52cf7b3be002c794e770` and current head; its tree is identical to the reviewed candidate.

Named follow-ups: localize the Windows workspace-ref timeout from the new scalar phase receipt if it recurs; localize the bundled-MCP packaging fixture's original over-60-second duration if it recurs (its synchronous assertions and cleanup returned before Vitest reported the elapsed deadline); the original factory/foreground phase delays, Gateway finalization delay and redacted recap mismatch remain unlocalized. Earlier unrelated relay, update-preview and Windows tool deadlines passed unchanged in later [hosted qualification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35866435705/attempts/2), but their triggers remain unproven. No CPU, infrastructure or cold-start cause is claimed.

### Existing measured test cost

These original-suite measurements are prior-source evidence. Case time sums individual reported durations; containing-command wall includes other files and preparation.

| Changed suite | Recorded cases | Case-time sum | Standalone file wall | Containing command wall |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| Worker inventory | 17 | 58.910 s | Not separately logged | 358.94 s; two-shard command |
| Task history | 16 | 29.841 s | Not separately logged | 1,108.85 s; two-shard command |
| Telegram native pipeline | 58 | 53.432 s | 59.89 s | 252.52 s; eight-file group |

Inventory and task-history timings come from the linked jobs at synthetic `11ff7d3`. Telegram timing comes from the earlier `5db14ad` fixture proof, which still contained the subsequently removed phase diagnostics. Recap before/after group wall times were 129.27 s / 102.99 s; the 22 recap case durations sum to 26.228 s before and 20.330 s after; standalone file wall time was not separately logged. These are observations, not a speedup claim.

The historical incident's exact triggering lifecycle event remains unproven. This PR repairs demonstrated database lifecycle boundaries; it does not claim deployment or live incident recovery.
